narrative.summary: The International Association of Insurance Supervisors (IAIS) is the global standard-setting body for insurance supervision. In July 2025, after a public consultation on a draft, it published an Application Paper on the supervision of AI that explains how its Insurance Core Principles apply to insurers' use of AI systems, covering governance and accountability, robustness, transparency and explainability, and fairness; it adds no new requirements.
narrative.review_notes: The IAIS application papers and its digital innovation pages were checked in November 2026. Not yet confirmed from the full official text: the wording of the final Application Paper, which is described here from the IAIS release, the consultation page, the final-paper webinar slides and the resolution of comments.

instruments.official_title: Application Paper on the supervision of artificial intelligence
instruments.english_title: Application Paper on the supervision of artificial intelligence
instruments.summary: Supporting material for insurance supervisors on applying the IAIS Insurance Core Principles (ICPs) to insurers' use of AI systems, covering consumer protection and prudential soundness. It uses the OECD definition of an AI system, focusing on systems with autonomy and adaptiveness rather than traditional mathematical models, and calls for a proportionate, risk-based supervisory approach. Its topics are governance and accountability (including human oversight and management responsibilities), robustness, safety and security, transparency and explainability, and fairness, ethics and redress; it states that insurers must assess whether acquiring or using third-party AI systems amounts to outsourcing of critical services. The IAIS states it adds no new requirements and that no changes to the ICPs are needed.
instruments.current_status: Final Application Paper published by the IAIS on 2 July 2025 after public consultation on a draft (18 November 2024 to 17 February 2025). Application Papers do not include new requirements; implementation is subject to the proportionality principle.

membership_note: IAIS members are insurance supervisors and regulators, not governments: a voluntary membership organisation of supervisors from more than 200 jurisdictions, constituting 97% of the world's insurance premiums. No country list is shown, so its documents are not attached to individual countries.
